scan.attacker: Website User (All role) unless guest path

findings.title: Authenticated SQL injection in client.get_count via unsanitized doctype (and filter keys) with no permission check
findings.description: frappe.client.get_count is @frappe.whitelist() for every logged-in user and calls frappe.db.count with the client doctype and filters with no has_permission/only_for check. db.count interpolates dt into from `tab%s` with % formatting. An attacker closes the identifier with a backtick and injects UNION/boolean/time-based SQL; the numeric result of UNION ... ORDER BY 1 DESC is returned as the count, enabling character-by-character exfiltration of __Auth password hashes and other tables. Filter dict keys are also concatenated inside backticks (and coalesce second args after `[`) in build_conditions, providing additional injection points. Distinct from client.get_value (checks has_permission(doctype) first and injects via fieldname), DatabaseQuery string filters (get_list path with sanitizers), bulk_update.update, and get_badge_info (different whitelist; patching those endpoints does not fix client.get_count).
findings.impact: Any Website User can extract password hashes, TOTP-related rows, and other database contents through the JSON count response, enabling offline cracking and account takeover. Even without SQLi, unrestricted counts of privileged DocTypes are an authorization failure.
findings.attack_path:
1. Authenticate as Website User (guest signup enabled by default).
2. POST /api/method/frappe.client.get_count with doctype set to a backtick-breakout payload such as: User` WHERE 0 UNION SELECT ORD(SUBSTRING(password,1,1)) FROM `__Auth` WHERE name='Administrator' AND fieldname='password' ORDER BY 1 DESC -- 
3. Template becomes select count(*) from `tabUser` WHERE 0 UNION SELECT ORD(...) ORDER BY 1 DESC -- ` so the UNION row sorts first and is returned as message.
4. Repeat ORD/SUBSTRING positions to recover the hash. Alternate: inject via filters JSON object keys into build_conditions backtick/coalesce wrapping.
findings.remediation: Require frappe.has_permission(doctype, 'read') before counting. Stop formatting doctype/filter keys into SQL; validate doctype against DocType names and bind identifiers with a strict allowlist. Prefer DatabaseQuery/get_list for permission-aware counts.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not on the prompt already-reported list. Not the same endpoint as get_value, get_badge_info, bulk_update.update, or DatabaseQuery string filters. Concurrent injection pass called it same-class near-miss; overturned because those patches do not touch client.get_count and get_value still gates on doctype read.

findings.title: Authenticated SQL injection in calendar.get_events via client field_map into ifnull() filter fieldnames
findings.description: frappe.desk.calendar.get_events is @frappe.whitelist() and builds start_date/end_date as ifnull(%s, ...) % field_map.start/end from attacker JSON. Those strings are used as filter fieldnames. DatabaseQuery.prepare_filter_condition detects 'ifnull(' in the fieldname and emits the raw string as column_name without backtick wrapping. sanitize_column's ifnull branch only rejects blacklisted keywords as exact whitespace-separated tokens, so space-free payloads with /**/ comments and functions like if()/sleep()/updatexml() pass. Pass fields=["name"] so the payload is not also placed into SELECT (where sanitize_fields is stricter). Event is role All readable, so Website Users reach get_list. Distinct from event.get_events user= IDOR and from DatabaseQuery raw string filters.
findings.impact: Any logged-in Website User can run time-based or error-based SQL against the database (password hashes, secrets) through calendar event queries.
findings.attack_path:
1. Authenticate as Website User.
2. POST /api/method/frappe.desk.calendar.get_events with doctype=Event, start/end date strings, filters=[], fields=["name"], and field_map JSON whose start value is a space-free injection such as: 1,if(1=1,sleep(5),0))OR/**/ifnull(1
3. Server builds fieldname ifnull(1,if(1=1,sleep(5),0))OR/**/ifnull(1, '0001-01-01 00:00:00'), sanitize_column allows it, prepare_filter_condition uses it raw, and the Event list query executes the injected SQL.
4. Use SLEEP/boolean or updatexml/EXTRACTVALUE-style payloads to exfiltrate __Auth or other tables.
findings.remediation: Allowlist field_map.start/end/title against meta fieldnames before formatting. Never put client strings into ifnull() SQL. In prepare_filter_condition, do not special-case ifnull( to skip identifier quoting; reject non-identifier fieldnames. Harden sanitize_column to treat ifnull templates as unsafe unless they match a strict regex of known field identifiers.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not on the already-reported list. Distinct from event.get_events user= calendar IDOR (different file/method/bug). Distinct from DatabaseQuery string-filter class: entry is field_map→ifnull unwrap, not a raw string filter element.
